root_cause.path: ApiBackfillRangeAcquisitionService::buildWindowCheckpoints() built every row from the single window telemetry entry returned by PublicApiEodBarsAdapter::fetchYahooFinanceBarsRange(); that entry is the aggregate of all tickers of the window (buildYahooRangeAggregateTelemetry), and the per-ticker request results were consumed into the aggregate and not retained
leaks: SUCCESS row http_status = $telemetry[final_http_status] ?? $telemetry[http_status]: the last non-null status any ticker saw in the window (a failing neighbour's 400/404), depending on iteration order
every row without a failure context (SUCCESS, and FAILED by a missing requested date) attempt_count = $telemetry[attempt_count]: the sum of the attempts of all tickers of the window
root_cause.measured_before_fix: raw red_before_fix.txt: four of the five new guards failed — 400 instead of 200; the same success row read [SUCCESS,400,6], [SUCCESS,404,4], [SUCCESS,400,5] when only its neighbours changed; 5 instead of 3; 4 instead of 2

files.change: buildYahooRangeAggregateTelemetry() additionally exposes ticker_request_telemetry: for each ticker the attempt_count and final_http_status of its own request (first request entry of the ticker wins). The window aggregates (attempt_count, final_http_status, http_status, ...) are unchanged and stay on the window telemetry.

buildWindowCheckpoints() reads the row's SUCCESS http_status and its attempt_count fallback from the ticker's own request entry; the window aggregate is no longer a source for any checkpoint-row field

not_changed: failed rows' http_status (already from their own failure context)
implementation_change.slip_fixed_before_testing_finished: my first edit read $ownRequest before assigning it (success status null); fixed by moving the assignment, caught by the new guards before any other work depended on it
